input.text: Silk Street is Beijing's most famous bargaining arena. It began in the nineteen eighties as an outdoor market of silk sellers along this street — foreigners discovered it, word spread, and the stall vendors eventually moved into a bright eight-floor mall you see today, keeping the old name and the old game. The rule of the house: the first price is an opening move, not a number. Start at a third of it, smile, walk away slowly, and watch the price fall with every step. Silk scarves and tailor-made shirts are the classics; tailors here can measure you and deliver a fitted coat in days. The upper floors drift into electronics and souvenirs — quality varies wildly, so buy what you can judge. No haggling skill needed to enter; it's the best free entertainment in Beijing anyway. Set a budget before you go in. Everyone says that. Everyone ignores it.
